Hi Marta — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then more detail and next steps below.

- Worst-case delete propagation (metadata only): up to 72 hours across async replication for EU-region pairs during high-load windows. Typical is <4 hours.
- Snapshots: we keep point-in-time snapshots immutable for a defined snapshot-retention window (configurable per tenant for Dedicated/Private). Deletions create tombstones that are eligible for prune after tombstone TTL; snapshots taken before the delete preserve the data until snapshot retention expires.
- Legal holds: supported. When a hold is applied we mark the relevant objects and they are excluded from prune waves; we record hold application time, owner, and reason in the audit log.

I'm looping Laura (SRE) and Marissa (Customer Success) for tech detail and to draft a short SLA excerpt for the PoC. If you can share the expected dataset size and retention target (e.g., 30/90/365 days), we'll propose the exact config for the PoC.

Hi all — adding the SRE perspective and a few specifics so your audit team has concrete numbers. TL;DR: design is conservative and intended to be auditable.

1) Propagation windows:
- Metadata delete marker propagation across replicated journal and object indices: typical 1-4 hours, worst-case 72 hours if replication backlog + region failover occurs.
- Full object expunge (data wipe from cold offsite replicas): prune waves run daily; objects marked for prune are queued, and physical expunge across all replicas completes within 7 calendar days after prune initiation under normal operations; worst-case (rare) we provision up to 14 days for cross-region reconciliation.

2) Snapshots vs tombstones:
- We take immutable snapshots every 24 hours for backups. Snapshots are immutable for the configured snapshot-retention period (e.g., 30/90/365 days). A deletion performed after a snapshot does not retroactively remove the snapshot copy; only when the snapshot retention lapses will that point-in-time copy be removed.
- Deletions place a tombstone in the live index immediately; tombstones are visible in metadata queries. The prune process respects snapshot boundaries — we never prune a snapshot-covered object until snapshot retention expires or is explicitly overridden by a retention policy.

3) Legal hold and audit evidence:
- Holds are a metadata overlay: applying a hold toggles a 'retain' flag on object records and prevents them from entering prune waves. Holds are recorded in our audit log with: actor, timestamp, scope (object IDs / account / path), and reason.
- For audit deliverables we can export: hold history CSV, prune-wave logs, replication status reports, and a snapshot manifest showing which snapshots contain the object in question.

Attachments I am including: dr-ttl-chart.png (visual of PRUNE -> EXPUNGE windows) and a short PDF excerpt from our backup policy (backup-policy-snippet.pdf).

Notes and caveats:
- If BrightPeak requests an immediate, manual expunge across all replicas for compliance, that is an operational action with a runbook and will require a scheduled maintenance window; we will provide the runbook and estimated timelines.
- During region failover we may rely on the most recent consistent snapshot available; that can affect the perceived delete window if a snapshot taken before deletion is used for failover.

Hope this helps — happy to hop on a quick 30-min call to walk the security team through the artifacts.

Laura Bennett
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Hi Marta — quick update and attachments.

1) Tombstone/expunge: after expunge completes we remove object payloads from all replicas. We do retain a limited metadata footprint (expunge event and object id hash) in the audit index for forensic traceability for up to 1 year; payloads are not recoverable once expunged. We can contractually extend metadata retention if required for legal reasons, subject to agreement.

2) Sample audit export: attached brightpeak-ma-plan.md includes a redacted CSV snippet demonstrating a hold being applied and a subsequent prune cycle skipping the object (columns: timestamp, object_id_redacted, hold_flag, prune_stage, actor).

3) PoC config: confirmed — we will stand up the PoC with daily immutable snapshots and a 90-day snapshot retention by default. Marissa will send the mutual action plan with an appendix listing the PoC retention settings and the small SLA excerpt (non-binding for PoC).
